title: Cyclotomic Cosets: Hidden Subgroup and Quantum Sieving Algorithm for Prime-Power Moduli
authors: Mathias Boucher, Pierre-Alain Fouque, Yixin Shen
abstract: The Learning With Errors (LWE) problem is a fundamental assumption in post-quantum cryptography. Regev established a quantum reduction from LWE to the Dihedral Coset Problem (DCP). Later, Brakerski et al. introduced the Extrapolated Dihedral Coset Problem (EDCP), proving its equivalence to LWE. However, unlike DCP, EDCP no longer admits a coset structure. This limits the direct application of techniques for hidden subgroup problems.   In this work, we introduce the Cyclotomic Coset Problem (CCP), a cyclotomic generalization of DCP that preserves an exact hidden-subgroup structure. Let $ζ_p$ be a primitive $p$-th root of unity, let $π=ζ_p-1$, and write $q=p^t$ and $L=t(p-1)$. We work over $R_q=\mathbb Z_q[ζ_p] \cong \mathbb Z[ζ_p]/(π^L)$, where the isomorphism follows from the total ramification identity $(p)=(π)^{p-1}$. We exploit the resulting $π$-adic ideal chain to construct a quantum sieve that successively reduces phase states modulo $π^{L},π^{L-1},\ldots,π$. For every fixed prime $p$ and modulus $q=p^t$, our algorithm solves the CCP in time and sample complexity $2^{O_p(\log n\log q)}$, using polynomial quantum space. The sieve also applies to uniform EDCP and Gaussian S|LWE>, yielding quasi-polynomial time algorithms for all the above problems when $q=\text{poly}(n)$. This extends the power-of-two EDCP sieve of Bai et al. (CRYPTO 2025) to a cyclotomic setting.   However, we emphasize that our result does not, by itself, yield a quasi-polynomial-time algorithm for standard LWE, because the currently known reduction produces only a limited number of approximate CCP states.
summary: This paper introduces the Cyclotomic Coset Problem (CCP) as a structured generalization of known hard problems in post-quantum cryptography, like the Dihedral Coset Problem. The authors develop a novel quantum sieve algorithm that solves CCP efficiently over cyclotomic rings. This work extends quantum algorithmic techniques to a broader class of algebraic structures relevant to lattice-based cryptography.
main_problem: The paper addresses the difficulty of applying Hidden Subgroup Problem (HSP) techniques to the Extrapolated Dihedral Coset Problem (EDCP) because EDCP lacks a direct coset structure.
main_result: The authors introduce the Cyclotomic Coset Problem (CCP) and develop a quantum sieve that solves CCP in time $2^{O_p(\log n\log q)}$ for fixed prime $p$ and modulus $q=p^t$.
method: The core method involves constructing a quantum sieve that successively reduces phase states across the $\pi$-adic ideal chain within the cyclotomic ring $R_q = \mathbb{Z}_q[\zeta_p]$.
model_or_system: The mathematical model is based on the cyclotomic ring $R_q = \mathbb{Z}_q[\zeta_p]$, which generalizes the structure used in the Dihedral Coset Problem (DCP). The quantum computation is performed on states defined over this ring structure.
key_observables: The primary observables are the quantum states associated with the CCP, and the success probability of the quantum sieve.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the prime $p$, the power $q=p^t$, the dimension $n$, and the error parameters $\alpha$.
main_assumptions: The result does not yield a quasi-polynomial-time algorithm for standard LWE because the known reduction only produces a limited number of approximate CCP states.
figures_summary: Figure 1 provides an overview comparing the contributions between $	ext{LWE}_{n,q,\alpha}$, $	ext{DCP}_{n,q}$, $	ext{CyLWE}_{n,q,p,\alpha}$, and $	ext{CCP}_{n,q,p}$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the algebraic framework over the cyclotomic ring $R_q$, then develops the quantum sieve algorithm for CCP, and finally shows how this solver can be used to achieve quasi-polynomial time algorithms for related problems like uniform EDCP and Gaussian S|LWE>. The structure builds from the algebraic generalization (CCP) to the algorithmic application.
why_interesting: While the focus is on number theory and cryptography, the development of quantum sieving techniques over structured rings like cyclotomic extensions represents a sophisticated application of quantum algorithms to abstract algebraic structures, which has parallels in quantum simulation of lattice models.
